pr.title: [Coverage][MCDC] Adapt mcdc to llvm 19
pr.description:
Related issue: #126672 

Also finish task 4 at #124144 

[llvm #82448](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/82448) has introduced some break changes into mcdc, causing incompatibility between llvm 18 and 19. This draft adapts to that change and gives up supporting for llvm-18.
pr.author: ZhuUx

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, MC/DC coverage instrumentation followed the LLVM 18 ABI. MIR coverage info recorded `CondBitmapUpdate { id: ConditionId, value: bool, decision_depth }` and the doc said it was "eventually lowered to `llvm.instrprof.mcdc.condbitmap.update` in LLVM IR." Codegen passed `(fn_name, hash, cond_loc, mcdc_temp, bool_value)` to that intrinsic. Decisions were sized in bytes: `*mcdc_bitmap_bytes += (1_u32 << decision.num_conditions).div_ceil(8);`, and `TestVectorBitmapUpdate` received `bitmap_bytes` plus `bitmap_index`. `ConditionId::NONE` was `Self::from_u32(0)` and condition IDs began at 1. Decisions were limited to `const MAX_CONDITIONS_IN_DECISION: usize = 6;`, with over-limit conditions downgraded to ordinary branch spans.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incompatible transformation is retaining the pre-PR LLVM-18 MC/DC lowering and sizing when targeting LLVM 19: emitting/consuming `llvm.instrprof.mcdc.condbitmap.update` with `(id, value)`, passing a byte count to `tvbitmap_update`, deriving bitmap positions from `ConditionId` with 0 as the NONE sentinel, and limiting a decision to 6 conditions. Under LLVM 19 the condition-bitmap intrinsic is gone, the TV-bitmap signature drops `bitmap_bytes`, condition IDs are `i16` with `ConditionId::START = 0` as a real node, the temp variable accumulates a test-vector index instead of a condition bit location, and decision mappings carry an end bitmap index. The corrected transformation replaces condition-id/value updates with `CondBitmapUpdate { index, decision_depth }` and, in codegen, `load mcdc_temp; add cond_index; store mcdc_temp`, computes per-branch test-vector offsets with `calc_test_vectors_index`, sizes the bitmap in bits/test vectors, and maps the decision to `bitmap_idx + num_test_vectors`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions with boolean control-flow decisions compiled with `-Cinstrument-coverage -Zcoverage-options=mcdc` for an LLVM 19 toolchain: `if`/`while` guards, `&&`/`||` combinations, non-tree decisions such as `(a || b) && c`, nested decisions, macro-expanded/inlined conditions, and decisions with more than 6 conditions (e.g. 7-way `&&`). Also includes degraded cases where a decision cannot be instrumented and must fall back to ordinary branch mappings.
analysis.summary: This PR adapts Rust's MC/DC coverage instrumentation from the LLVM 18 ABI to LLVM 19. The reusable knowledge is a set of coupled invariants: condition IDs vs. test-vector indices, byte vs. bit bitmap units, start vs. end bitmap indices, false-before-true traversal order, and span containment. It is a version-compatibility migration, not evidence that a runtime coverage bug was reproduced.
analysis.trigger: Switching MC/DC coverage instrumentation to LLVM 19, or changing any one of the coupled representations (ConditionId vs. test-vector index, bytes vs. bits, start vs. end bitmap index) without updating the others.
preconditions: The target LLVM is 19 or newer; the patch asserts `MCDC intrinsics require LLVM 19 or later`.
MC/DC coverage is enabled with `-Zcoverage-options=mcdc` together with instrumentation coverage.
A function contains a boolean decision whose conditions/branches are instrumented.
The decision's condition graph is a valid DAG/tree reachable from `ConditionId::START`; `calc_test_vectors_index` asserts no untouched nodes remain.
The total test-vector count fits the bitmap limit derived from `i32::MAX`, and a decision has at most `i16::MAX` conditions.
pitfalls: Do not use 0 both as a real condition id and as the 'no next condition' sentinel. The patch changes `ConditionId::NONE`/`from_u32(0)` to `ConditionId::START`/`from_usize(0)` and changes next ids to `Option<ConditionId>`; a missing next id (`None`) is an end of the decision.

Do not mix bitmap bytes with test-vector bits. The old code sized decisions with `(1 << num_conditions).div_ceil(8)` bytes; the new code tracks `mcdc_bitmap_bits` as the total number of test vectors/bits.

Do not write the start index where LLVM 19 expects the end index. Branch updates use the decision start `bitmap_idx`, but `MappingKind::MCDCDecision` is built with `bitmap_idx + num_test_vectors` as the end index.

The temp variable must be initialized to zero and updated by accumulating `cond_index`: `let new_tv_index = self.add(current_tv_index, cond_index); self.store(new_tv_index, mcdc_temp, align);`. Treating the index as a bit position or condition id breaks verification.
Traversal order matters. The code visits false before true: 'First check the false next to ensure conditions are touched in same order with llvm-cov.'
End nodes are sorted in descending `num_paths` order (`usize::MAX - *num_paths`) to match LLVM's bitmap-size optimization; a different order changes test-vector numbering/reporting.

LLVM requires the decision span to contain all condition spans. Macro expansion can violate this, so the patch unions branch spans and substitutes the joint span when `decision_span` does not contain it.

When a decision is degraded (too many conditions, too many test vectors, or unbranchable spans), its conditions must be emitted as ordinary branch mappings, not MC/DC mappings; the patch warns via `MCDCExceedsConditionLimit`/`MCDCExceedsTestVectorLimit`.

The limits changed: per-decision limit is `i16::MAX` because LLVM uses `i16` condition ids, and total test vectors are bounded by `i32::MAX` because LLVM indexes the bitmap with `i32`. The old 6-condition limit is obsolete.
analysis.testStrategy: Use coverage UI/coverage tests gated to LLVM 19 with `//@ min-llvm-version: 19`, `-Zcoverage-options=mcdc`, and `//@ llvm-cov-flags: --show-branches=count --show-mcdc`. Assert both `.cov-map` mappings and `.coverage` text. Cover: (1) a 7-condition `a && b && ... && g` decision that is now fully instrumented (the updated test runs it with all-false and all-true inputs, expecting 7 conditions and 14.29% MC/DC); (2) non-tree `(a || b) && c` to exercise indegree/path bookkeeping and false-before-true ordering; (3) nested decisions and inlined conditions; (4) decisions exceeding limits to verify fallback to branch mappings and warnings. Check that `MCDCDecision` records an end-style `bitmap_idx` while `MCDCBranch`/`CondBitmapUpdate` use the start/test-vector offsets. Do not claim execution; compare compiler outputs/test expectations.
